required_stages.description: Allocate a fresh contiguous (n, m) output of x's dtype inside run().
One kernel pass that reads each element of x once and writes it once to the transposed position of the output, with edge tiles handled so that no out-of-range element is read or written.

forbidden_substitutions.message: A PyTorch view-transpose followed by contiguous()/clone() performs the whole operator on the host.
Host-side transpose/permute of x; if its result is returned or copied, the whole operator is done by PyTorch.
A host-side copy inside run() is either a second data pass or the transpose itself.
Returning the input or a view of it violates the fresh-output requirement.
No dtype conversion is allowed anywhere in matrix_transpose.

required_evidence.message: No kernel-level store found; the transpose must be done by a kernel.
No evidence of transposed addressing or an in-tile transpose primitive.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (n, m) tensor must be freshly allocated inside run(), contiguous row-major, and must not share storage with x

timing_boundary.notes: Everything inside run() is timed: the output allocation and the single transpose kernel. No cached state, no untimed re-layout or prepacking of x, no host-side copies.
